name: Ruun
hail: Pupil, we are old, and we have much to teach. Will you listen?
Greetings, Pupil. We are Ruun. Our world is old, and we would rather teach than keep.
Hello, Pupil. Settle in. There is a great deal to go over.
close: That is enough for one lesson. Ruun.
Study well, Pupil. We will be here while we can.
finding: {part} Work it through yourself. It is worth the effort.
Here is something we learned the slow way: {part}
{part} Read it twice. The second time is the lesson.
sighting: {part} We point it out so you can learn to see it.
Under our easy sky, we saw this: {part}
{part} There is always something to learn from a sky.
archive: From our long schooling, freely given: {part}
{part} We give this away gladly. Knowledge kept is knowledge lost.
{part} Take it, and teach it on.
We have taught this to our own. Now, to you: {part}
culture: {part} An old world learns to say such things plainly.
Our world is old, and we have made peace with that. {part}
{part} That is part of the lesson too.
request: From the old to the young: {part}
What have you learned that we did not? Here is where we would start: {part}
verdict: We have thought it through for you: {part}
{part} We will explain our reasons, if you wish.
{part} There is a lesson in it.
accord: {part} We will explain any term you do not follow.
